project_type: FileForgeWorkbench -- a Rust Cargo WORKSPACE (crates/*). ISPF-inspired cross-platform file editor / mainframe workstation. egui desktop shell (ff-desktop) over narrow model crates (here: ff-help).
build_system: Cargo workspace. Crates touched: ff-help (crates/ff-help), ff-desktop (crates/ff-desktop). The OWNER runs the authoritative full gate via a custom `cargo gate` (nextest, whole-workspace) OUTSIDE Kiro. Agents must NOT run the full suite.
test_framework: Rust built-in #[cfg(test)] unit tests, run with `cargo test -p <crate> <focused_name>`. (The full suite uses cargo-nextest via `cargo gate`, owner-only.)
build_command: cargo check -p <crate>   (SCOPED to the touched crate)
test_command: cargo test -p <crate> <focused_name>   (SCOPED + bounded; quick focused tests only)
verification_instructions: Per .kiro/steering/gate-policy.md: on every change run the SCOPED trio on the touched crate(s) and read logs back -- `cargo check -p <crate>`, `cargo clippy -p <crate> -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p <crate> -- --check` -- PLUS quick scoped tests `cargo test -p <crate> <focused_name>`. Agent verification is COMPILE-ONLY + quick scoped tests; NEVER run `cargo test` whole-workspace, `cargo nextest`, `cargo gate`, or `cargo full-gate` (they wedge this machine's terminal). The owner runs the full `cargo gate` manually and is the authority on a green full run. TDD (.kiro/steering/testing.md): write the FAILING test FIRST, confirm it is RED (scoped), then implement to GREEN; every test carries a `// Validates: Requirement X.Y` comment. Read any build/test log back before declaring success (terminal exit codes are unreliable on this machine; verify by effect).
environment_constraints: Terminal: use the clean pwsh7 form `C:\tools\powershell7\pwsh.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "..."`; do NOT chain with `;` on the raw path; prefer the dedicated read/grep/edit tools over the shell for inspection. A machine-wide execution proxy captures command output to a result file under C:\Users\A142367\.kiro\terminal-log\results\ -- READ that file for the real result. Do NOT run dev servers or the full gate. Long scoped builds may exceed a short timeout -- redirect to a log and read it.
contribution_requirements: ASCII-ONLY in all Markdown/help/steering/docs and pattern-matched source (.kiro/steering/documentation-charset.md): no em dash (use --), no curly quotes, no Unicode arrows (use ->). rust-standards.md: types UpperCamelCase, fns snake_case; NO source .rs file over 400 non-test lines (split tests near ~200); functions <= ~40 lines; no unwrap/expect in library code (use ? / Option); derive Debug on public types; `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` clean. framework-conformance.md mechanism 1: ONE command dispatch front door (dispatch_command_string) and ONE help-display seam (open_help); do NOT add a second dispatcher or a bespoke `if upper == "..."` intercept. The CR-NR-119 design verdict is explicitly NO framework change. extension-terminology.md: new code uses 'extension' not 'plugin' (do not introduce new plugin-named items; only rename plugin->extension when already editing such an item).
key_patterns: ff-help topic format: a `.help.md` file holds one or more topics delimited by `<!-- TOPIC: cmd:<ROOT> -->` then `<!-- TITLE: <Human Title> -->`, body is standard Markdown with a `## Description` section whose FIRST paragraph is the one-liner (see help/commands/session.help.md for cmd:SAVE/CANCEL/END/UNDO/REDO). HelpTopic exposes `body()`. TopicKey::command(name) -> `cmd:<name>` and preserves a space (so `cmd:FILE CATALOGS` is valid). The shell owns one Arc<HelpTopicRegistry> at `self.help.registry`; `open_help(arg)` + private `display_help_topic(&key)` in shell/help.rs are the single display seam (dynamic index/function_keys generated, miss -> index-with-message). resolve_help_argument (ff-help commands.rs) special-cases KEYS->feature:function_keys and CONFIG/CONFIGURATION->feature:configuration BEFORE the cmd: fall-through -- Req 22.8 requires cmd:KEYS / cmd:CONFIG to take precedence for the root reach-path. builtin_ffcmd_roots() (shell/alias_reader.rs) = BUILTIN_FFCMD_LADDER_VERB_ROOTS + BUILTIN_WORKSPACE_VERB_ROOTS (command_config/mod.rs) + the two recovery menus' option roots (menu_workspace/defaults.rs); EnvironmentRegistry::root_commands("FFCMD") (shell/environment_registry.rs) returns it. The front door dispatch_command_string (shell/dispatch.rs) runs `=`-strip -> rewrite_verb_to_root -> run_command_prelude -> resolve_target -> run_command_ladder; split_verb_arg (shell/helpers.rs) splits on first whitespace only (hence two-word roots cannot be --help-detected: deferred, Req 15.9). Alias editor: AliasRowEdit (alias_editor_panel/state.rs) has a `description` field persisted via the user override; open_alias_editor -> load_effective_alias_rows -> load_rows; SAVE serialises the working rows, so display-time inheritance must NOT fill the stored description (Req 9.2). Display seams: render_data_row (alias_editor_panel/rows.rs, Description cell hint_text) and alias_editor_screen_model/alias_table + command_configurator_screen_model (shell/screen_providers.rs).
